content: This medication may interact with certain laboratory tests, such as allergy skin tests or urine corticosteroid levels, potentially leading to inaccurate test results. It is important to inform your healthcare provider or laboratory personnel if you are using this medication before undergoing any tests. In the event of an overdose, if the individual exhibits severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, immediately call emergency services (911 in the United States). For less severe cases, contact a poison control center without delay. U.S. residents can reach the poison control center at 1-800-222-1222, while Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. If you miss a dose of this medication, consult your doctor or pharmacist promptly to establish a new dosing schedule. Do not double up on doses unless specifically instructed by a healthcare professional. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not dispose of medications by flushing them down the toilet or pouring them into a drain unless explicitly directed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed, following local disposal regulations or pharmacy guidelines. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the medication is safe, effective, or appropriate for your specific situation. Always consult your healthcare provider for comprehensive information tailored to your health needs. Before using hydroxyzine, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, cetirizine, levocetirizine, or any other substances. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could trigger allergic reactions or other complications. Hydroxyzine may also cause a condition known as QT prolongation, which affects the heart's rhythm. The risk of QT prolongation may increase if you have certain medical conditions or are taking other medications that can prolong the QT interval. Low potassium or magnesium levels in the blood can also elevate this risk, particularly if caused by diuretics, severe sweating, diarrhea, or vomiting. This medication may cause dizziness, drowsiness, or blurred vision. Alcohol or cannabis use can exacerbate these effects. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or engaging in activities requiring alertness or clear vision until you are certain you can perform them safely. Limit alcohol consumption while using this medication. Older adults may be more susceptible to side effects such as drowsiness, confusion, constipation, difficulty urinating, or QT prolongation. Children may also be more sensitive to the drug's side effects. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary, and it is not known whether it passes into breast milk. Consult your doctor before breastfeeding. Drug interactions may alter the effectiveness of this medication or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs as well as herbal supplements, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Check the labels of all your medications, especially allergy or cough-and-cold products, as they may contain ingredients that cause drowsiness.
